title: How to Switch from Demostack to Storylane
summary: Moving from Demostack to Storylane? This guide covers what happens to your demos, the migration steps, and what your team gains after switching.
body_markdown:
If you're on Demostack and considering a switch, this guide covers what migration looks like: what happens to your existing demo environments, the steps involved, and what changes after.


Tool Pricing (2026) Best for Storylane advantage


Storylane Free plan, paid from $40/mo, self-serve signup GTM teams that need demo velocity and multiple formats without an engineering-heavy build Four demo formats with stable URLs and step-level edits, so a product release does not force a rebuild


Demostack From ~$55,000/yr (10 users, one app); no free trial Large enterprises with technical teams that need high-fidelity clones of a backend-heavy product Demostack clones the live product, so every update means recreating clones; Storylane decouples the demo from the app


Demostack pricing above is drawn from published Storylane comparison content.


## Why teams move from Demostack to Storylane


If you're still comparing options, Storylane's[full comparison with Demostack](https://www.storylane.io/blog/storylane-vs-demostack) and its[list of Demostack alternatives](https://www.storylane.io/blog/demostack-alternatives) cover features, pricing, and which fits your team.


If you've already decided to move, the most common reasons teams make the switch are:


- **Every product update forces a rebuild.** Demostack clones your live product, so when the app ships a change, existing clones have to be recreated from scratch. One account executive noted in a G2 review that any change to the product means recreating all existing clones. Storylane builds demos from screens, so a release does not trigger a rebuild cycle.
- **Demo links break when clones are edited.** Editing a clone can break the links you have embedded across your website, sales decks, and email templates, which means chasing down and updating every embed. Storylane keeps stable URLs, so edits do not break where the demo already lives.
- **Setup is engineering-heavy and slow.** Demostack's fidelity comes from cloning the full environment, which takes real setup time and technical resources, plus maintenance after every update. Storylane's no-code capture lets a GTM team create a demo without engineering support.
- **It is priced and scoped for enterprise only.** Demostack starts around $55,000 per year for a small user count and one app, with no free trial to validate first. Storylane offers a free plan and paid plans from $40/mo, so you can prove out the motion before scaling spend.
- **One format, when teams need several.** Demostack centers on cloned sandbox environments. Storylane covers screenshot, video, HTML, and sandbox formats plus hubs, so different buyers get the format that fits how they want to evaluate.

## What happens to your existing Demostack demos?


Your demos carry over. Share the links with Storylane, the screens get captured and rebuilt across the formats that fit each buyer, and a CSM reviews the result with you. The migration is also when you move off the clone-and-rebuild cycle to stable, editable demos that survive your next product release.


## Step-by-step: switching from Demostack to Storylane


**1. Audit your active Demostack demos**


List the demos and cloned environments currently embedded on your site, shared in outbound sequences, or used in sales calls. These are your migration priorities. Older or one-off demos can follow later.


**2. Start a Storylane trial or book a migration call**


Sign up at storylane.io or book a demo directly. For teams with multiple active demos, the migration call is faster. Your CSM is assigned from the start and handles the heavy lifting.


**3. Send your Demostack links**


Share the URLs. Storylane's automation captures your screens and rebuilds the guided, interactive steps in your workspace.


**4. Review and improve with your CSM**


Your CSM walks through the migrated demos with you. This is where you configure[lead capture forms](https://www.storylane.io/blog/lead-forms-in-storylane-capturing-your-most-promising-leads) , set up[viewer identification and CRM routing](https://www.storylane.io/blog/guide-to-lead-attribution-for-interactive-demos) , add branching paths, and pick the right format for each demo.


**5. Replace your embeds and go live**


Swap the Demostack links for Storylane's. Storylane supports[embedding across your full go-to-market stack](https://www.storylane.io/blog/product-demos-on-multiple-platforms) : website, email sequences, sales decks, LinkedIn outreach, and review sites like G2.


## What you gain after switching


- **No rebuild cycle when the product ships.** Storylane demos are built from screens with stable URLs and step-level edits, so a product release does not force you to recreate clones or fix broken embeds.
- **Demos any team can create, without engineering.** No-code capture means marketing, sales, and CS can build and update demos in minutes rather than waiting on technical resources for every change.
- **Multiple formats from one platform.** Screenshot, video, HTML, and sandbox demos plus hubs let you match the format to how each buyer wants to evaluate, instead of a single clone-based approach.
- **A self-serve path and pricing that starts small.** A free plan and paid plans from $40/mo let you validate the motion before scaling spend, rather than committing to a large annual enterprise contract up front.
